contributions.headingText: Primary cutaneous peripheral T-cell lymphoma (pcPTCL) NOS is a poorly characterized group of T-cell lymphomas not meeting the criteria for any specifically defined primary cutaneous T-cell lymphoma entity; i.e. it is a diagnosis of exclusion.
9709/3 Primary cutaneous peripheral T-cell lymphoma, NOS
2B0Z Primary cutaneous T-cell lymphoma of undetermined or unspecified type
Acceptable: primary cutaneous peripheral T-cell lymphoma, unspecified.

Disseminated skin lesions are predominantly located on the trunk and limbs {29573477; 32997839}, whereas solitary tumours are more commonly found on the skin of the legs, arms, and (occasionally) head and neck {29573477; 32997839}.

Most patients present with disseminated plaques, papules, or tumours {32997839; 29573477; 12750155}. About one third present with solitary lesions {32997839; 29573477}.

The skin lesions can show ulceration (~15% of cases) {32997839}. Although pcPTCL-NOS is limited to the skin at the time of diagnosis, systemic involvement commonly develops later during the course of the disease.

pcPTCL-NOS is exceedingly rare, and it mostly arises in adults in their sixth decade of life. Presentation in the paediatric age group has also been described {32997839; 29573477; 12750155}. There is a male predilection (M:F ratio: 3:1) {12750155; 29573477; 32997839}.
Pathogenesis is largely unknown, although gains of chromosomes 7q, 8, and 17q and loss of chromosome 9p21 have been reported {19710685}.

Because pcPTCL-NOS is a diagnosis of exclusion, distinct and characteristic histopathological and immunophenotypic features are lacking; however, features of any other cutaneous T-cell lymphoma entity can be observed, albeit outside the typical context. The skin shows diffuse or nodular dermal infiltration of cohesive sheets of mostly medium-sized to large lymphoid cells {12750155; 27498959; 30296539; 32997839}. The subcutis is commonly involved {32997839}. A mild and focal epidermotropism is found in approximately one third of cases {32997839}. Angiocentric/angiodestructive features and folliculotropism are rare {12750155; 30296539; 32997839}.

Immunophenotype

The tumour cells are positive for CD2 and CD3 {32997839}. The most common phenotype is CD4+/CD8− {12750155; 32997839}. About one third show a CD4−/CD8− phenotype, and approximately 10% are CD4+/CD8+ {32997839}. Cytotoxic markers (TIA1 and granzyme B) are mostly negative (75%) {32997839}. Aberrant expression of CD20 can occur {32997839}. The proliferative activity is moderate to high (30–90%). PD1 expression (> 40%) can be found {32997839}. EBV is negative {32997839}.

Very rare cases of primary cutaneous T-cell lymphoma with a T follicular helper (TFH) cell phenotype have been described {22508770; 26282465}. Further data are needed to better characterize this entity. Therefore, primary cutaneous T-cell lymphomas with a TFH-cell phenotype (defined by the expression of at least two TFH-cell markers: PD1, ICOS, CD10, BCL6, CXCL13) should currently be placed in this group, i.e. pcPTCL-NOS with a TFH phenotype.
Fine core needle biopsy usually does not provide sufficient material to make this diagnosis.
Not generally relevant. TR gene rearrangements can be informative but are not specific.

Essential: diffuse or nodular dermal infiltrates of atypical T lymphocytes; no extracutaneous involvement of the lymphoma at time of diagnosis; a diagnosis of exclusion – does not meet the diagnostic criteria for defined cutaneous T-cell lymphoma entities.

Desirable: molecular studies to exclude other specific entities in selected cases.

pcPTCL-NOS is staged according to the International Society for Cutaneous Lymphomas (ISCL) / Cutaneous Lymphoma Task Force of the European Organization of Research and Treatment of Cancer (EORTC) system {17339420}.

The prognosis of pcPTCL-NOS is poor, with mean overall survival times between 27 months {29573477} and 5.6 years {27498959}. Some studies showed a better prognosis in solitary lesions {29573477}; this might provide a rationale for radiotherapy in such cases {12750155; 29573477; 32997839}. B symptoms, multifocal lesions, and systemic involvement are unfavourable prognostic factors {27498959}. In disseminated lesions, multiagent chemotherapy is used, although it may not be effective {12750155; 32997839}.
